challenger_routes.why_considered: A goal of the form 'Write the text T to the file X and save the report to Y' returned status PASS__COMPOSED_CAPABILITY_CHAIN with pass=True after writing those 11 bytes into Y. X, the file the goal actually named, was never created on disk and the front door reported the goal done. Composition is attempted at exactly the two moments where the primary path has already failed, and both call sites returned the chain's own verdict untouched. The gate that catches this, promised_artifact_errors, had already run; its result was discarded.
challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: apply the gate that already exists to the fallback before it may report success. Two supporting defects were found by measuring the same family. (1) Template key order for the repair capabilities is output_path, source_root, test_argv, test_paths, and test_argv is derived FROM the test paths, so counting a derived argv as a competing claim cancelled the role against itself: exclusivity emptied a correct test_paths, the fallback then assigned every file in the sentence, source included. (2) That masking hid a second defect: _repo_paths only checks that a path RESOLVES under the root, so 'test command /usr/bin/python3 T' bound usr/bin/python3 as a test file and the adapter rejected it with FILE_INVALID. Both are fixed generally: an argv is not a claim, and a role list may only name files that exist. Measured: the false PASS becomes FAIL_CLOSED__PROMISED_ARTIFACT_MISSING naming the exact missing file; test_paths on the route-admission sentence returns exactly the named test; test_paths on the strict-progress sentence returns exactly the named test with no interpreter. route_frontier.negative_search_summary: No external package or new mechanism was needed.  The live challengers were a general postcondition that recomputes the file -- rejected because an in-place edit leaves nothing to recompute from -- trusting the exit status, rejected because it is the producer grading its own work, and snapshotting the file before the run, rejected because it adds a second source of truth the verifier would then have to trust.

recursive_obs.why_selected_route_is_fastest_sufficient: The blocker was one function stating one promise, and sed already supplies every other promise the same discipline allows, so the work was to enumerate them rather than to build anything.  The dominant alternative was a general postcondition that recomputes the whole file, which loses because an in-place edit consumes its own oracle and there is nothing left to recompute from.  The second, trusting the command's exit status, loses because that is the producer grading its own work and is the exact thing the postcondition table exists to avoid.  The third, snapshotting the file before the run, loses because it adds a second source of truth the verifier would then have to trust.

stop_condition: Holds: the fifteen-row edit census is fifteen of fifteen against the real commands, the certified wrong answer is gone, every new postcondition is pinned able to fail, the unprovable edits are refused with the file byte-identical, and the 212 tests that passed before still pass.
weakens_existing_guard: No fail-closed rule is weakened.  `_post_sed` gains promises and refuses every shape it still cannot state, including `1d`, `$d` and a substitution between two texts.  `_post_chmod` admits exactly `+x` and `-x` on one operand and refuses a numeric mode and `a+x`, because "make the file executable" states the owner bit and nothing about the other two.  Three tests that pinned refusals were rewritten harder rather than deleted: the invariant that an edit never deletes the file now covers the served sentences too, and the position test now pins both the served prepend and the still-refused bare insert.
